:::{#def-fixed-effect}
#### Fixed effect

A **fixed effect** is a model term
whose coefficient the model treats as an unknown constant,
such as the effect of a specific treatment
or the mean of a specific group;
the goal is to estimate that particular value
[@rocke2021epi204; @gelman2006data, Chapter 11].
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-fixed-effect}
#### A treatment fixed effect

In a trial comparing a new blood-pressure drug with a placebo,
let $X = 1$ for the drug group and $X = 0$ for the placebo group,
and suppose that the mean systolic blood pressure (in mmHg) is
$$
\E{Y|X=x} = \b_0 + \b_1 x,
$$
with $\b_0 = 120$ and $\b_1 = -8$.
Both coefficients are fixed effects:
each is a single constant that applies to every participant.
The mean in the drug group is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{Y|X=1}
&= \b_0 + \b_1 \cdot 1
&& \text{(substitute $x = 1$)}\\
&= 120 + (-8) \cdot 1
&& \text{(substitute the coefficient values)}\\
&= 112
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
